refreshNote: Data refreshes are scheduled through GitHub Actions. Scheduled workflows can start later than their configured times, so timestamps show when this project actually fetched and published each source.

sources.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.scheduleDescription: Checked approximately every 10 minutes (external timer plus a GitHub Actions schedule as backup). Actual run times may be delayed.
sources.provides: Recorded earthquakes worldwide from the USGS 'all earthquakes, past 7 days' GeoJSON summary feed: magnitude, depth, location, time, tsunami flag and PAGER alert level where supplied.
sources.coverage: Global recorded earthquakes. Completeness is highest in the United States; small earthquakes elsewhere may not be listed.
sources.coverageLimitations: Detection and publication timing vary by region and network. Magnitudes, locations and other parameters can be revised after publication, and some events are deleted.
sources.licenseOrAttribution: Data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). USGS-authored data is generally in the U.S. public domain; please credit USGS.

sources.source: GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.name: GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.geometryLevel: point, polygon and country (varies by event)
sources.scheduleDescription: Checked approximately every 20 minutes (external timer plus a GitHub Actions schedule as backup). Actual run times may be delayed.
sources.provides: Alerts for major earthquakes, tropical cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts and wildfires, with the GDACS alert level (Green / Orange / Red) and affected countries when supplied.
sources.coverage: Global, but limited to events large enough to trigger GDACS automatic or manual assessment.
sources.coverageLimitations: GDACS is an alert and coordination system. Its alert levels are model-based estimates of humanitarian impact and can change as assessments evolve. Many events are represented by a single representative coordinate; the affected area may be much broader.
sources.licenseOrAttribution: Source: GDACS (European Commission Joint Research Centre and UN OCHA). See the GDACS terms of use; attribution required.
sources.notes: Event list from sample; 4 of 6 events have a published affected area.

sources.source: NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System
sources.name: NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System
sources.scheduleDescription: Checked approximately every 60 minutes (external timer plus a GitHub Actions schedule as backup). Actual run times may be delayed.
sources.provides: Near-real-time satellite active-fire / thermal hotspot detections (MODIS and VIIRS) for the past 7 days, with detection time, sensor, confidence and fire radiative power.
sources.coverage: Global land areas observed by the satellites. Each location is observed only a few times per day.
sources.coverageLimitations: Detections are thermal anomalies, not confirmed wildfires: they can include agricultural burning, industrial heat sources, gas flares, volcanic activity or other hot surfaces. Clouds, smoke and satellite overpass timing cause gaps. Near-real-time data is typically available within about 3 hours of observation, but this varies by product.
sources.licenseOrAttribution: NASA FIRMS data courtesy of NASA's Land, Atmosphere Near real-time Capability for EOS (LANCE). NASA data is openly available; please acknowledge NASA FIRMS.
sources.requiresSecret: FIRMS_MAP_KEY (optional; if absent the project uses the public FIRMS active-fire text files)

sources.source: U.S. National Weather Service — Active Alerts
sources.name: U.S. National Weather Service — Active Alerts
sources.scheduleDescription: Checked approximately every 10 minutes (external timer plus a GitHub Actions schedule as backup). Actual run times may be delayed.
sources.provides: Active NWS watches, warnings and advisories with event type, severity, urgency, certainty, effective/expiry times and affected areas.
sources.coverage: United States and its territories only. No coverage outside the United States.
sources.coverageLimitations: Zone-based alerts are drawn using simplified zone outlines, so boundaries are approximate. Alerts may be issued, updated or cancelled between project refreshes. Always follow official NWS and local authority instructions.
sources.licenseOrAttribution: Source: U.S. National Weather Service (NOAA). NWS information is in the U.S. public domain.
sources.notes: 1 active alert(s) could not be drawn yet because their zone outlines have not been fetched; they will appear after later refreshes.

sources.source: NASA EONET — Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker
sources.name: NASA EONET — Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker
sources.geometryLevel: point, track or polygon (varies by event)
sources.scheduleDescription: Checked approximately every 60 minutes (external timer plus a GitHub Actions schedule as backup). Actual run times may be delayed.
sources.provides: Open natural events curated by NASA from other agencies — wildfires, severe storms, volcanoes, floods, landslides, dust and haze, snow and temperature extremes — with a link to the original source.
sources.coverage: Global, but limited to events that NASA EONET curators have catalogued; many smaller events are not included.
sources.coverageLimitations: EONET is a curated catalogue, not a warning service: events can be added or closed with a delay, and it assigns no severity level. Storms are shown at their latest reported position. Earthquakes are excluded here because USGS is used directly; sea and lake ice events are excluded as not place-relevant. Some events overlap with GDACS.
sources.licenseOrAttribution: Data courtesy of NASA's Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET); each event links to its original source agency.

sources.source: Internet disruptions (e.g. Cloudflare Radar Outage Center)
sources.name: Internet disruptions (e.g. Cloudflare Radar Outage Center)
sources.scheduleDescription: Not connected. A future integration would refresh through GitHub Actions using a repository secret.
sources.provides: Not connected. Planned: annotated Internet outage events.
sources.coverageLimitations: API access requires a token that must never be exposed in browser code. Licence, caching and redistribution terms must be confirmed first. Disruptions are often country- or network-level and are not city-specific.
sources.unavailableMessage: No connected Internet-outage source. Coverage and location precision vary by network and region.

sources.name: Electricity outages (regional provider plugins)
sources.scheduleDescription: Not connected. Each regional provider would declare its own refresh interval.
sources.provides: Not connected. There is no single free, standardized global electricity-outage feed; outages are published separately by utilities and grid operators.
sources.coverageLimitations: Provider plugins must use official structured feeds where legally and technically permitted, and declare their coverage area.
sources.unavailableMessage: No electricity-outage data source is currently connected for this location.

sources.source: Airport / airspace disruptions (e.g. FAA NAS Status)
sources.name: Airport / airspace disruptions (e.g. FAA NAS Status)
sources.provides: Not connected. Planned: airport delay programmes and airspace restrictions from official aviation authorities.
sources.coverageLimitations: Airport status describes the airport or airspace only, not the surrounding city. Source terms must permit automated use.
sources.unavailableMessage: No airport or airspace disruption source is currently connected for this location.

sources.source: Official public-health notices (e.g. WHO Disease Outbreak News)
sources.name: Official public-health notices (e.g. WHO Disease Outbreak News)
sources.provides: Not connected. Planned: official outbreak notices associated with a country or region, as supplied by the source.
sources.coverageLimitations: Notices are usually country- or region-level and are not personal health or travel advice.
sources.unavailableMessage: No official public-health notice source is currently connected.
